items.title: Drew Doughty opens up about free agency, trade noise, asking price, injury
items.summary: At age 36, Drew Doughty is ready for a pay cut. But he wants to go back to Cali in 2027-28. Luke Fox caught up with the longtime Kings defenceman about free agency and more.
items.body: TORONTO — Rare is the occasion when a hockey player openly floats a dollar figure that would likely convince him to sign a new deal with his hockey team. But Drew Doughty is nothing if not unique, and the impending unrestricted free agent has no designs on playing coy with the club he loves. As the newly minted captain of the Los Angeles Kings — the club that drafted him second overall more than 18 years ago — sits in a Scotiabank Arena visitors’ room stall, he considers fellow multi-Cup-winning superstars like Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin in Pittsburgh and the idea of sticking with one team till the very end. “I only want to wear one sweater. I want to live the rest of my life in L.A., even when I’m done playing. I mean, I’ve already lived half of my life in L.A. I’ve lived there for… this is my 19th year. So, I think it's amazing to be able to stay with one team. But I see where you're going with that,” says the ever-candid Doughty. “That's why, I mean, if they can sign me for, say, $4 to $6 million or something like that — with me still playing the most minutes on the team — I think that’s a hell of a deal for them.” Them is general manager Ken Holland and the L.A. brass, who announced prior to puck drop that they will take a wait-and-see approach with their outspoken, gap-toothed, universally beloved icon during 2026-27, the final season of No. 8’s eight-year, $88-million contract. At age 36, Doughty is ready for a pay cut. He hasn’t put up a fuss over conceding power-play quarterback duties; Erik Gustafsson currently runs PP1. items.body: Washington loses fourth straight, NHL’s all-time goals leader has just one through 20 games WASHINGTON -- Alex Ovechkin had a difficult time enjoying his latest record-breaking moment because it came in another Washington Capitals loss, and yet another game in which he didn’t score a goal. Ovechkin’s 763rd assist to surpass Nicklas Backstrom ’s Capitals record was mostly a footnote following a 6-3 loss to the Buffalo Sabres at Capital One Arena on Thursday. It was the fourth consecutive loss for Washington, which allowed at least five goals in each of the defeats, and fell to a disappointing 10-10-0 through its first 20 games. “We just have to keep fighting,” Ovechkin said. “Sometimes things don't go your way, but we just have to keep fighting and stay with it.” Ovechkin has been fighting it all season. The NHL’s all-time leader with 930 goals has scored just one through his first 20 games and was held without one for the 15th straight game Thursday. That’s the longest goal drought of his 22-season NHL career, exceeding one of 14 games from Nov. 22-Dec. 20, 2023. The 41-year-old left wing has six points (one goal, five assists) this season, including just two (both assists) in his past 12 games. “Chances are there,” Ovechkin said. “It’s just sometimes you hold the stick too tight. Just stick with it and keep working.” After Ovechkin announced on Oct. 5 that this will be his final season in the NHL, the Capitals hoped to send him off with another run at the Stanley Cup. They appeared in good position to do it following an active offseason in which they added two three-time 30-goal scorers in Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou , versatile forward Boone Jenner and stay-at-home defenseman Vincent Desharnais . items.title: Gauthier’s goal streak ends at 10 games as Ducks get shut out by Avalanche
items.body: DENVER — Brock Nelson had two goals and an assist as the Colorado Avalanche blanked Anaheim 4-0 on Thursday night, ending Cutter Gauthier 's goal-scoring streak at 10 games for the Ducks. Scott Wedgewood made 26 saves in his 13th career shutout and first this season. He became the first goaltender to keep Gauthier from scoring since Vancouver's Leevi Merilainen on Oct. 27. The 22-year-old left winger was the first NHL player with a goal in 10 consecutive games since Teemu Selanne set the Anaheim record with an 11-game run in 1997. Gauthier had four hat tricks during the streak, including Tuesday night in an 8-6 defeat at St. Louis. Gauthier also went without a point for the first time since Oct. 22 at New Jersey, stopping a 12-game streak. Devon Toews had a goal and an assist, and Nicolas Roy also scored for the Avalanche, who bounced back from a 4-1 loss Wednesday night at scuffling Utah. Martin Necas added two assists. Lukas Dostal stopped 24 shots for the Ducks, who have lost four of five since a five-game winning streak.

Gallagher took an awkward fall after getting tangled up in front of the net and left the game in obvious discomfort at 11:30 in the second period with Vancouver down 3-1. items.title: Mark Stone sets new Golden Knights all-time points record
items.body: Mark Stone stands alone on the Vegas Golden Knights ' all-time leaderboard. The team's long-time captain set a new franchise points record with an assist on Victor Olofsson's power-play goal in the second period of Thursday's game against the Dallas Stars. The assist gives Stone 418 points for his career, surpassing the previous record set by Jonathan Marchessault, who had 417 points in a Golden Knights uniform. Stone, a Winnipeg native, has scored 147 goals and 270 assists for Vegas after being traded from the Ottawa Senators at the 2019 trade deadline. So far this season, Stone has kept a pace of 21 points (11 goals, 10 assists) in 23 games played for the Golden Knights.

items.title: Rangers finding identity among strong start to season
items.summary: GREENBURGH, N.Y. -- Mike Sullivan's rides to the rink have been far less stressful in his second season as the New York Rangers coach than they were in his first.
items.body: Playing physical, faster in Sullivan’s second season behind bench GREENBURGH, N.Y. -- Mike Sullivan's rides to the rink have been far less stressful in his second season as the New York Rangers coach than they were in his first. That happens when a coach is confident his team has an identity and will consistently play to it, as the Rangers have for a large enough percentage of their first 22 games this season. "When I drive to the rink, I feel fairly confident that I know the type of game that the players are going to put on the ice," Sullivan said. "Some nights are better than others but that's just part of it, that's just the human element of sports, but our intentions, our compete level, our mindset, things of that nature, are in the right place most nights, if not all. As a coach that's a good feeling when you're driving to the rink." Sullivan's rides were never easy last season, especially at home, where the Rangers turned Madison Square Garden into their own house of horrors in his first season in New York, winning 14 of 41 games, the No. 1 reason they were last in the Eastern Conference with 77 points. This season, the Rangers (13-8-1) have won nine of 11 home games, 13 of 22 overall, including three in a row and six of their past seven. They're third in the Metropolitan Division and in the middle of a five-day break before playing the Carolina Hurricanes at home Sunday. items.title: Support from Flames says plenty of Huberdeau’s reputation
items.summary: Everything you need to know about how beloved Jonathan Huberdeau is in the Flames organization was on full display when the 33-year-old was warming up for his first AHL game. Eric Francis has the story.
items.body: CALGARY - For nine lonely months, Jonathan Huberdeau wondered if he’d ever return to the game that’s given him everything. So when he stepped onto the ice for his first game since hip resurfacing surgery, his Calgary Flames teammates wanted him to know he wasn’t alone. Everything you need to know about how beloved Huberdeau is in the Flames organization was on full display Wednesday night at the Dome when the 33-year-old winger was warming up for his first AHL game with the Wranglers. A quick glance up along the glass allowed Huberdeau to spot Mikael Backlund , Ryan Strome and Joel Hanley, standing with their young children, alongside his own son. Given the early-morning skates, solo workouts, and the uncertainty of wondering if his hip would ever cooperate again, it was an awfully powerful moment. "It warms my heart, because that means they actually really care about each other - it's not lip service," said coach Ryan Huska, who was on hand with his coaching staff to witness the moment. "He really means a lot to them, and it goes the other way as well. It was cool to see, for sure. "There isn't a better team guy that you'd ever be around than Jonathan Huberdeau, and he's rubbed off in so many different ways to all of our players. When they see the struggles that he went through to get himself to the point to play, they're really proud of him, and they are in his corner 100 per cent." When Huberdeau looked up towards the owners’ suite, he saw members of what the coaches joke is his Boy Band: Matt Coronato, Morgan Frost, Joel Farabee, Zayne Parekh, as well as Matvei Gridin and Brennan Othmann. items.title: Lane Hutson leads Canadiens to gutsiest win of season
items.summary: The Hurricanes tried to push them. But Lane Hutson and the Canadiens didn’t just get up and push back, they pushed the Hurricanes over in a way they haven’t been able to in recent memory.
items.body: This was Lane Hutson as we’ve never seen him before — doubled over, gasping for the air that had been knocked out of him by the type of hit he’s so rarely been on the receiving end of since he jitterbugged his way into the NHL at the end of the 2023-24 season. Hutson was uncharacteristically lackadaisical, atypically unaware of Shayne Gostisbehere’s presence. He never saw it coming. But it was Gostisbehere and the Carolina Hurricanes who, in the end, were on the end of an unforeseen outcome. Because Hutson bounced back up from that second-period hit that left him winded and eventually took everyone’s breath away. First with a stunner of a tying goal late in the third period. And then with the winner that made it 2-1 Montreal Canadiens in overtime to cap their gutsiest performance of the season. “Everyone stepped up,” Hutson told reporters at Lenovo Center. That was right after Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis referred to it as a win that made them “better as a team.” It’s exactly what we were thinking with each passing minute of the game, as the Canadiens finally bore their teeth against this hungry pack of wolves. Oh sure, they beat the Hurricanes three times last regular season and once more at the start of the Eastern Conference Final last spring. But none of those games looked like this one, with the Canadiens pinching all the pressure points the Hurricanes typically have a firm grasp of. That they did it less than 24 hours after registering a bounce-back win against the red-hot Devils in New Jersey, that they did it missing several key players, and that they did it against a Hurricanes team that’s still sitting with the NHL’s best points percentage (.795) despite the loss, said everything about how much their character has grown since that lopsided playoff series.

The Minnesota Wild had to be concerned a bit with their goaltending entering this season, considering one half of their outstanding tandem, Filip Gustavsson , was going to miss some time recovering from hip surgery in May. That would put the burden on Jesper Wallstedt , who started 10 of the Wild's 11 games in the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs after starting consecutive games only twice during the regular season. So, could Wallstedt, who turned 24 on Nov. 14, carry the load by himself? Judging by the first quarter of the season, he's answered any questions. Wallstedt has started 20 of Minnesota’s first 23 games and is 16-2-3 with a 1.95 goals-against average and .926 save percentage. His play has helped the Wild (17-3-4) take a nine-point lead atop the competitive Central Division. He's allowed two goals or fewer 15 times, and his .934 save percentage at even strength ranks third among NHL goalies who have started at least 10 games (Linus Ullmark, Ottawa Senators, .964; Daniil Tarasov, Detroit Red Wings, .941). Wallstedt’s strong play has made him NHL.com’s pick to win the Vezina Trophy as the League’s top goalie thus far. He received 60 voting points, including five first-place votes, from a panel of 15 NHL.com staff members. items.body: TORONTO -- Drew Doughty remains optimistic he and the Los Angeles Kings will agree to a new contract before he becomes an unrestricted free agent after this season. “I'm still confident we are going to get a deal done,” Doughty said after the Kings morning skate Thursday. “I don't want to go anywhere, they know that. I don't think they want me to go anywhere.” Doughty was named captain of the Kings on Sept. 16, taking the place of Anze Kopitar, who retired after last season. The 36-year-old defenseman, who was the No. 2 pick by the Kings at the 2008 NHL Draft, has played his entire career for Los Angeles and has 717 points (166 goals, 551 assists) in 1,298 games. The two-time Stanley Cup champion (2012, 2014) is in the final season of an eight-year, $88 million contract he signed with Los Angeles on July 1, 2018. He can become an unrestricted free agent this coming July 1. “It doesn't bother me,” Doughty said. “I haven’t thought about it at all. It (stinks) if you get injured or something, you start thinking, like the other day I blocked a shot and I thought ‘Oh, this isn't good for my next contract’ but I don't think about it. I don’t care.” Winner of the 2016 Norris Trophy voted as the best defenseman in the NHL, Doughty has also been a staple for Team Canada. He won Olympic gold for his country in 2010 and 2014, and helped Canada win the World Cup of Hockey 2016 and the Four Nations Face-Off in 2025. He was a member of Team Canada at the 2026 Winter Olympics, winning a silver medal. This season, he has eight points (one goal, seven assists) in 19 games. items.summary: Two Oilers streaks were put to bed in a stingy loss to the Lightning on Thursday. The defeat marked Edmonton’s first road regulation loss of the season, and the first game in which Connor McDavid was unable to crack the score sheet.
items.body: At some point, the Edmonton Oilers were going to lose a road game in regulation this season. And at some point, Connor McDavid was going to play a game in the 2026-27 season without picking up a point. Well, the Tampa Bay Lightning killed two birds with one stone Thursday, knocking Edmonton off by a 3-1 score and shutting out McDavid, snuffing both the Oilers' pursuits on one salty Florida night. “In the end, they were better than us and capitalized on their opportunities,” Oilers head coach Mike Babcock told reporters in Tampa. “I didn't think either team had a ton of opportunities here today.” This game was similar to Edmonton’s trip-opening, 1-0 win at Toronto. There was a bit more offence in this one, but it was two teams locking ‘er down for most of the night. “It was a pretty stingy game,” agreed Oilers defenceman Matias Ekholm. “They get a huge power-play goal to get the (1-0) lead, and the lead is so big in these types of games, since the other team has to open up a little bit. We weren't able to recover, really. “Give them credit; they played good. Their goalie (Andrei Vasilevskiy) was good. I thought we played okay, but I think we have another level." Edmonton is now 1-22-1 in the Lightning’s barn since the 2011-12 campaign. Talk about a House of Horrors: the Oilers never win here but somehow have a much better record across the state in Sunrise, at the home of the Panthers. How good has Edmonton been this season? items.title: Wild’s Quinn Hughes exits in win over Flames
items.body: The Minnesota Wild picked up a 4-1 win over the Calgary Flames on Thursday, but it may have come at a price. Superstar defenceman Quinn Hughes exited late in the contest after he was on the receiving end of a hit from Flames forward Adam Klapka midway through the third period. Wild head coach John Hynes had no update on Hughes' status after the game, but he did confirm to reporters the defenceman was not removed by the concussion spotter. Hughes headed straight to the locker room after the hit and did not return for the remainder of the game. He made his presence felt before leaving, as he had a goal and an assist in 23:24 of ice time. Hughes' two points on Thursday bring his season totals to eight goals and 26 assists over the first 24 games of the season. The Wild also overtook the Oilers for the best record in the league by beating the Flames, as they now sit atop the overall standings with a 17-3-4 record. Minnesota's next game is against the Canucks on Saturday, and we will have to wait and see if Hughes is back to take on his former team in Vancouver for a second time this season.

items.summary: Even though the Toronto Maple Leafs lost their eighth straight contest on Thursday, they don’t need to worry about the health of their captain.
items.body: Even though the Toronto Maple Leafs lost their eighth straight contest on Thursday, they don't need to worry about the health of their captain. Auston Matthews took an awkward fall at the end of the Maple Leafs' 4-3 shootout loss to the Los Angeles Kings and was in visible discomfort as the buzzer sounded. The once 69-goal scorer collided with Quinton Byfield trying to enter the zone and took a tumble onto the ice. He was grabbing his side while grimacing as he slowly made his way to the bench before the shootout. Matthews still managed to take the Maple Leafs' first shootout attempt following the injury scare. Following the game, Matthews said he just "felt kind of weird" after the collision, but "after a couple of minutes it was fine." Matthews has 13 goals and 19 assists for 32 points through 24 games this season. items.title: Connor McDavid’s season-opening point streak ends at 23 games
items.body: For the first time this season, Connor McDavid failed to find the scoresheet. McDavid had his 23-game point streak come to an end as the Edmonton Oilers lost to the Tampa Bay Lightning 3-1 on Thursday. The 23-game tear was the longest point streak of McDavid's career, and tied for the fourth-longest to open a season in NHL history. Wayne Gretzky holds the record for the longest season-opening point streak at 51 games, which he set in the 1983-84 season. McDavid will finish his epic run with a staggering 13 goals and 42 assists for a league-leading 55 points. Thursday's loss to the Lightning also snapped a six-game Oilers win streak. Lightning goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy came within 1:39 of recording his first shutout of the season. Nikita Kucherov, John Carlson and Ilya Mikheyev scored for Tampa Bay, which improved to 10-1 at home. Devon Levi stopped 17 shots for Edmonton, and Shakir Mukhamadullin scored for the Oilers. Edmonton lost for the first time in regulation on the road this season, falling to 10-1-1. Following a scoreless first, the Lightning broke the ice on their second power play chance of the game. Brayden Point slipped a pass from the corner down low to Jake Guentzel who swung behind the net and zipped a pass to Carlson in the middle slot for a one-timer at 13:29. Beckman, 25, will have the opportunity to play in his first NHL contest since April 2024 as a member of the Wild. Drafted by Minnesota in the third round seven years ago, the winger broke the 100-point mark in his last full junior season as a Spokane Chief, generating some hype with his high end shot and making a quick Wild debut at age 20. Suiting up for 22 more games over the years with three assists, at this point he has made most of his impact in the AHL. Proving himself as a reliable scorer for the Iowa Wild with defensive shortcomings, not uncommon for non-prospects who light up the AHL, the Saskatoon native Beckman made stops with the Utica Comets and Bridgeport Islanders. He put together a 30-goal campaign last season for the New York farm club prior to catching on as part of the Avalanche organization. items.body: David Banks-Imagn Images David Banks-Imagn Images Opinion: Wasn't Jim Hiller Supposed To Help The Toronto Maple Leafs Become A Better Defensive Team? Adam Proteau Partner Nov 20, 2026 12:11 AM Published Nov 20, 2026 12:11 AM Updated Nov 20, 2026 12:45 AM New NHL coaches are often the opposite of the bench bosses they've replaced, but has Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller really been different, or in any way better, than Craig Berube? As is often the case when NHL teams change coaches, the organization's choice for a new coach is someone with a significantly different philosophy than that of their predecessor. A team that failed with a coach who was more rigid or autocratic in their approach almost always ends up replaces him with a more player-friendly bench boss — and vice versa. So, when the Toronto Maple Leafs fired coach Craig Berube at the end of last season and replaced him with Jim Hiller, the idea was that Hiller would succeed at turning Toronto into a better defensive team than the one Berube tried to mold to fit his approach. Both go about their business in different ways, but has Hiller actually succeeded where Berube couldn't? But so far this season, Hiller hasn't delivered a much-improved defensive structure. In fact, the Maple Leafs have gone from allowing 3.6 goals per game under Berube to 3.52 under Hiller. items.body: Register Login Avalanche’s Gabriel Landeskog, Parker Kelly Fined By Brennan McClain | at November 19, 2026 5:00 pm The NHL’s Department of Player Safety has issued two separate fines from last night’s contest between the Colorado Avalanche and the Utah Mammoth. First, the DoPS fined Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog $5,000 (the maximum allowable) for cross-checking Mammoth forward Logan Cooley . The DoPS also fined Avalanche forward Parker Kelly $3,500 for high-sticking Mammoth forward Michael Carcone . There was an immediate expectation that Landeskog would face supplemental discipline. Early in the contest, Cooley attempted to hit Landeskog, and he ended up rolling over his back. Cooley attempted to stand up, but Landeskog repeatedly cross-checked him, even while he was on the ice, until he was eventually pulled off. The referees assessed Landeskog a double-minor for the incident. This isn’t the first time Landeskog has had a run-in with the Department of Player Safety. The former second-overall pick has been suspended four different times throughout his 13-year career, for 11 games total. Today’s discipline is his second career fine. The last time he was fined was during the 2014-15 season for punching the Minnesota Wild’s former captain, Mikko Koivu . Meanwhile, this is Kelly’s first time being fined. Still, like Landeskog, he’s faced discipline from the Department of Player Safety before. Toward the end of the 2023-24 campaign, Kelly received a two-game suspension for an illegal check to the head against Los Angeles Kings defenseman Andreas Englund . items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Minnesota Wild announced Thursday that goaltender Filip Gustavsson has been assigned to their AHL affiliate on a conditioning stint. He is expected to start for the Iowa Wild this Saturday against the San Diego Gulls. Gustavsson, 28, underwent hip surgery in the summer and started the season on injured reserve . In 2025-26, he went 28-15-6 with a .904 save percentage (SV%) and a 1.4 goals saved above expected (GSAx) with four shutouts in 50 games. This season will be the first in a five-year, $34-million contract extension that Gustavsson signed in October 2025. He will carry a cap hit of $6.8 million through the 2030-31 campaign. In six NHL seasons, the Skelleftea, Sweden, native is 111-74-26 with a .911 SV% and a 2.67 goals against average (GAA) in 219 appearances with the Wild and Ottawa Senators . He also has a 4-7 record with a .911 SV% and 2.67 GAA in 12 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. Gustavsson was taken in the second round of the 2016 NHL Entry Draft by the Pittsburgh Penguins . He spent two more seasons developing in Sweden’s top professional hockey league with Lulea HF before he moved to North America. In 2018, Gustavsson was traded to the Senators, along with Ian Cole, a first-round pick and a third-round pick in exchange for Derick Brassard. He spent parts of five seasons with their AHL affiliate, the Belleville Senators, where he posted a 45-39-8 record with an .898 SV% and 3.06 GAA in 95 appearances.

items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google Logan Thompson and Charlie Lindgren took the ice with new masks at Thursday’s morning skate — and for a good cause. The special goalie masks were designed in recognition of the NHL’s Hockey Fights Cancer Month and will be worn when the Washington Capitals face off against the Buffalo Sabres for Hockey Fights Cancer Night later this evening. The masks are a part of a Monumental Sports & Entertainment Foundation auction with proceeds benefiting cancer-related causes. Thompson’s mask is especially emotional as it was inspired by 14-year-old William Martel of King William, Virginia, who was diagnosed with brain cancer in December 2025. Martel, who lost vision in his left eye due to a germinoma tumor, first met Thompson in June 2026 while undergoing radiation treatment. Having admired Thompson’s goalie mask, Martel wanted his own radiation treatment mask to look just as “cool” and modeled its design after the Capitals goaltender’s mask. items.title: Report: Simon Edvinsson passed on multiple offer sheets to force exit from Red Wings
items.summary: Edvinsson must sign by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 to be eligible to play in the NHL this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The situation between the Detroit Red Wings and defenseman Simon Edvinsson keeps getting uglier. Edvinsson, 23, is currently a restricted free agent, having not yet signed an extension with the Red Wings following the completion of his three-year, entry-level deal last season. He must sign a deal by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 in order to be eligible to play in the NHL this season. According to Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli, Edvinsson has turned down offer sheets from multiple teams in order to deny Detroit the opportunity to match, putting pressure on the Red Wings to simply trade him before the December 1 deadline. “He’d love to be signed and playing,” a source told Seravalli. “But he no longer wants to play in Detroit and that would be the risk with an offer sheet.” Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff mentioned earlier this season that he has “zero interest” in trading Edvinsson. Horcoff may be forced to change his tune, or else risk losing Edvinsson for the season if nothing gets done ahead of the December 1 deadline. Detroit would still retain Edvinsson’s rights in that case, but would presumably receive less appealing trade offers for a player that could no longer play this season. Seravalli also pointed out that there is a daily cap penalty for the first year of a contract given to a restricted free agent after the start of the regular season, meaning the cap hit for this season on any deal Edvinsson may ultimately sign gets higher with each day he remains unsigned. Selected sixth overall by the Red Wings in the 2021 NHL Entry Draft, Edvinsson had nine goals and 16 assists for 25 points in 72 games with Detroit last season, while averaging just under 22 and half minutes of ice time.

items.body: Time is up on Simon Edvinsson ’s tenure with the Detroit Red Wings — the only question that remains is whether a trade will be executed prior to Dec. 1’s deadline or cost him the season. While interim GM Shawn Horcoff indicated as recently as last week that his intention was still to sign Edvinsson, that ship has sailed. Sources say multiple teams made overtures on offer sheets in an attempt end the saga but Edvinsson has chosen not to engage because he does not want to give Detroit an opportunity to match. “He’d love to be signed and playing,” one source said. “But he no longer wants to play in Detroit and that would be the risk with an offer sheet.” Ten of the 14 offer sheets signed in the NHL’s salary cap era have been matched by the team holding the restricted free agent, including both Leo Carlsson and Barrett Hayton last summer. The clock is ticking. Horcoff and the Red Wings seem comfortable making the Edvinsson camp sweat by taking it to the deadline, now just 12 days away. items.title: Bedard to remain out while Blackhawks weigh rehab vs. surgery
items.summary: The Chicago Blackhawks franchise player remain on the sidelines while the team decided on a course of action.
items.body: The Chicago Blackhawks ' franchise player remains on the sidelines while the team decides on a course of action. The Blackhawks are still receiving more information as they weigh rehab or surgery for Connor Bedard 's shoulder injury, head coach Jeff Blashill told reporters on Thursday. Bedard will remain out at least through Chicago's upcoming road trip, Blashill said. Bedard got hurt on a faceoff early in the third period of Tuesday night's 6-3 win over Toronto. The 21-year-old centre slammed his stick on the ice and held his right arm in front of him as he made his way to the locker room. The 2023-24 Rookie of the Year has 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) through 15 games. He became the second-youngest captain in Blackhawks franchise history at the start of the season. Anton Frondell stepped in as Chicago's No. 1 centre in practice on Wednesday, skating on a line with rookie Roman Kantserov and Tyler Bertuzzi. The 19-year-old Frondell has four goals and seven assists in 21 games this season.

items.body: Jets head coach Scott Arniel told reporters Thursday that the defenceman will be out for the next four to six weeks. DeMelo, 33, has been out since he suffered a lower-body injury in an 8-3 win over the Dallas Stars on Nov. 12. The London, Ont., native got his right leg caught under a falling Mikko Rantanen and went straight down the tunnel halfway through the first period. items.title: What would Russia’s 2027 World Junior roster look like?
items.summary: Russia’s roster would be deep up front and in the crease, but they’ll have to settle for exhibition events instead.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis The lead-up to the 2027 World Junior Championship in Edmonton and Red Deer has been anything but ordinary. Late last month, the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled that Russia was to be allowed immediately back into international competitions, starting with the World Juniors later this year. That meant Norway was getting pushed out despite earning a spot through the proper qualification process last winter. Then, nearly every single team said they would boycott playing against the Russians, with the Canadian government even outright banning visas to the players. In the end, the International Ice Hockey Federation announced that Russia would not partake in this year’s tournament before reinstating Norway. This seems like a situation that won’t go away quietly. But it made us wonder: what would Russia’s roster look like if they were to actually compete this year? They’re definitely stronger than Norway; having Russia instead would give the tournament a true best-on-best sense again. Canada’s roster isn’t going to be as strong as it was even last year when they finished with bronze. The Americans lack scoring depth, and Sweden’s going to be missing some of its top players who will stay in the NHL. Czechia will definitely be in the conversation for gold, and you can never count out Finland. There’s no doubt the Russians would be right in that medal mix, especially with their goaltending. At the same time, they’re a program that has struggled to deliver results at this tournament. items.body: Register Login Lightning Recall Jansen Harkins By Gabriel Foley | at November 19, 2026 9:50 am The Tampa Bay Lightning have added a forward to the lineup with four games left in their current homestand. Centerman Jansen Harkins has been recalled for the first time this season. Harkins broke camp with Tampa Bay and played in the first game of the season before being reassigned on October 7th. He has since appeared in 11 games with the AHL’s Syracuse Crunch. Harkins has recorded six points and four penalty minutes in those minor-league appearances. Harkins is in his first season in the Lightning organization after spending the last two seasons as a depth forward with the Anaheim Ducks. He spent much of that tenure in the NHL lineup, appearing in 106 games with Anaheim marked by 14 points and 49 penalty minutes. Harkins also appeared in 11 games with the San Diego Gulls where he scored a productive 17 points. His career has winded through depth roles, also taking him through four seasons with the Winnipeg Jets and one year with the Pittsburgh Penguins. Harkins’ call-up will serve as insurance as the team faces injuries to Conor Geekie , Brandon Hagel , and Zemgus Girgensons . Both Hagel and Girgensons are out day-to-day while Geekie was recently placed on injured reserve. Harkins won’t face much competition for a lineup role after Tampa Bay chose to ice 11 forwards and seven defensemen in Tuesday’s win over the Washington Capitals. Should the club want to return to a 12-forward lineup, Harkins’ would have a carved out role at fourth-line center between Jeffrey Viel and Scott Sabourin . That trio could operate as Tampa Bay’s bottom line with five more games on the schedule before the end of November.

items.summary: The PWHL’s takeover tour returns, seeing Halifax host three games over the 2026-27 regular season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL The PWHL is heading back on the road, announcing an expanded edition of the PWHL Takeover Tour for the league’s fourth season since first dropping the puck in January 2024. The 2026-27 Takeover Tour will see the league hit 19 markets across North America, bringing 24 games to markets outside teams’ home markets, with the aim of putting the league in front of more eyes and potentially testing the waters for future expansion. Several markets will host multiple dates this season. Halifax leads the way with three matchups, while Denver, Philadelphia, and Washington, D.C., will each host two games through the expanded calendar. All cities have been in the conversation about potential expansion at some point in the future. Including the multi-stop markets, the tour returns to 10 cities, including Buffalo, Calgary, Chicago, Denver, Edmonton, Halifax, Québec City, Raleigh, Washington, D.C., and Winnipeg. It will also visit new locales: Columbus, Hartford, Los Angeles, Nashville, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Saskatoon, Sunrise, and Tampa, with Hartford welcoming back professional women’s hockey for the first time since losing the Connecticut Whale of the PHF, before the league amalgamated to form the PWHL. Washington, D.C.’s Capital One Arena will host the first game on Jan. 2 between the Boston Fleet and Ottawa Charge, while the multiple stops in Halifax include back-to-back games on Feb. 2-3 and a final clash on March 21. The Takeover Tour schedule will conclude late in the season, with the New York Sirens battling the Toronto Sceptres on April 10 in Philadelphia. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Kucin Jr.-Imagn Images The Alex Ovechkin takes were equal parts strong and wrong three years ago. As of Dec. 29, 2023, his age-38 season, the Washington Capitals legend sat at six goals in 33 games and 828 for his career. Pundits began to wonder if his quest to eclipse Wayne Gretzky’s NHL-record 894 career goals would fall short – including me. I wrote about it in detail . Then Ovechkin did what he had done so many other times in his career and defied all laws of human aging. He heated up for 25 goals over his final 46 contests of 2023-24. In a magical 2024-25, as if fuelled by the hunger for Goal-G.O.A.T. status, he played like a younger man, ripping off an incredible 44 goals in just 65 games, overcoming a broken leg during the season and smashing Gretzky’s record. The 2025-26 season was house money, with ‘Ovi’ sprinkling in 32 more goals at 40 years old, swelling his career total to an unfathomable 929. After teasing retirement in the 2026 offseason, Ovechkin rejoined a stacked Caps roster for one final run at the Stanley Cup. As a bonus: he needed just 11 more goals to pass Gretzky for the most in NHL history across the regular season and Stanley Cup playoffs combined. And while it was unlikely we’d see another unicorn season like his 2024-25, it was reasonable to accept another 30 goals, give or take, if the Caps kept trotting Ovechkin out for entire power plays to unleash his one-timer. Liam O’Brien, Dmitri Simashev and Kevin Stenlund scored goals for the Mammoth. Sebastian Cossa made 30 stops. Mackenzie Blackwood tallied 25 saves for Colorado. "I mean, I'm going to try to keep it as normal as possible, treat him like another player, but I am going to be keeping a close eye on him for sure," Brian told NHL.com's Dan Rosen on Wednesday. For me personally, I don't know about for him, but since I got into this side of the game I've always been like, 'Man, it would be so cool to call his games.' It would be really meaningful to me. items.title: Canadiens end power-play drought in win, hand Hellebuyck 1st Devils loss
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Jake Evans scored the go-ahead goal, captain Nick Suzuki ended his team's long power-play drought and the Montreal Canadiens defeated the New Jersey Devils 3-2 on Wednesday night to halt a two-game skid. Connor Hellebuyck got a piece of Evans' shot with his glove but could not keep it out of the net. The goal with 13:43 left sparked “Go, Habs, go!” chants from the many Canadiens fans in attendance. Hellebuyck allowed three goals on 27 shots and lost for the first time in eight starts since joining New Jersey in a trade from Winnipeg in late October. Despite Timo Meier setting up a goal by Luke Evangelista and scoring on a breakaway fresh out of the penalty box, the Devils had their two-game winning streak snapped, losing for just the second time in their past nine. The Canadiens only trailed for 40 seconds after Evangelista's goal, as Alex Newhook got in on net and made a nifty move to beat Hellebuyck and tie it. After spending time practicing the power play on Tuesday and devoting significant conversation to what was going wrong, they came up empty on their first two chances. With Montreal's run at 0 for its past 14, a parade to the penalty box eventually came back to bite New Jersey. Suzuki drew a tripping penalty on Brenden Dillon, then deflected Lane Hutson's point shot in past Hellebuyck with 41.9 seconds remaining in the first period. Jacob Fowler stopped all 20 shots he faced in the second and third, finishing with 27 saves and avoiding what would have been his first time losing consecutive games this season. He and his teammates successfully killed a penalty in the final minutes to seal it. JJ Peterka and Pavel Zacha also scored for the Bruins, who snapped a three-game skid. Mason Lohrei and Morgan Geekie each had two assists. Daniil Tarasov, coming off a shutout of the Tampa Bay Lightning, made 27 saves, but couldn’t prevent Detroit’s sixth loss in seven games. Detroit's Lucas Raymond made it 1-0 at 16:58 of the first period. Keegan Kolesar knocked the puck loose in the neutral zone to set up a 2-on-1 break, and Raymond blasted Andrew Copp’s pass inside the left post for his ninth goal. Peterka tied the game at 2:47 of the second, cutting in from the left wing and beating Tarasov on the glove side. Zacha then gave the Bruins a 2-1 lead with a power-play goal at 11:48, putting in a rebound for his sixth of the season. Instead we’re not even in December and there’s already questions being raised . Toronto is 1-9-0 in their last 10, 27th in the NHL. Their offensive production has been acceptable, but it’s their other classic shortcomings which continue to hamper the group. Nearly two years ago today the Blues fired Drew Bannister 22 games into their season, although the coach had 76 total games behind the bench before the decision was made, counting the season prior. Considering everything at stake, one can’t rule out an abrupt change behind the bench sometime later this season before it is too late. items.body: Former goalie will broadcast forward’s next game against Flyers on Thursday The 49-year-old former NHL goalie has spent his entire life in the game, more than half of it in the League as either a player or broadcaster, but never before did he experience what he felt while in the stands at Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg alongside his wife, Melissa, and daughter, Brianna, watching his son, Tyler, score the game-winning goal in his NHL debut with the Ottawa Senators. "I mean, I've had some cool moments in my career; five shutouts in a row stands out," said Boucher, who set the NHL record for longest shutout streak (332:01) in 2003-04. "Win an eight-period game in Pittsburgh in the playoffs, five overtimes (in 2000). But this is better just because it's your kid, and we're all so proud of our children." Tyler Boucher was selected by the Senators with the No. 10 pick in the 2021 NHL Draft, but injuries and four surgeries, two on his knee and one on each shoulder, derailed the 23-year-old's journey to the NHL until he finally got there and scored at 4:04 of the second period to give Ottawa a two-goal lead en route to a 2-1 win. "I think what I'm most proud of with him, honestly, it's not that he played his first NHL game or that he scored, that's awesome stuff, but it's the story behind it and the resilience and perseverance and fight that he showed," Brian Boucher said. He then followed that up by scoring twice on the power play, 36 seconds apart, to complete his second career hat trick. His first PPG of the night would stand up as the game-winner. “Trying to keep it simple, a lot of volume shooting,” Gauthier said per NHL.com. “The more I get pucks on the net, if they’re not going in, they’re creating good opportunities for my teammates and creating chaos.” Two nights later, Gauthier notched another hatty in a 5-4 victory over the Vancouver Canucks , scoring shorthanded, on the power play, and at five-on-five. items.title: Reeling Penguins at crossroads as ‘Big Three’ era winds down
items.summary: It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud.
items.body: CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Pa. — It took Kyle Dubas more than three years, but the Pittsburgh Penguins general manager finally said the quiet part out loud. Asked Wednesday what gives him hope that his struggling team, which is mired near the bottom of the Eastern Conference and has three regulation wins through 20 games, can turn it around in time to salvage this season, Dubas turned philosophical. Yes, making the playoffs for a second straight year would be nice. Yet that's not the metric he will lean on to gauge progress. Dubas would like the team's younger players to take “major steps.” He'd like to see the iconic, aging core led by captain Sidney Crosby show it still has “gas left in the tank." He'd like some of the prospects he's acquired since taking over to make a push for NHL playing time. If those things can happen, Dubas believes the franchise will be on “the right track" regardless of where the Penguins wind up in the standings. Then, Dubas finished by using a phrase that included the one word he has consistently avoided uttering publicly since taking over in the summer of 2023. “This has been, I think rightfully, an unorthodox style of rebuilding a team because of the players that are here,” he said. items.title: Things we (think we) know: Oilers forging different identity under Babcock
items.summary: The Oilers are becoming a different team under Mike Babcock. They’re finding ways to win beyond McDavid and Draisaitl, playing a more complete brand of hockey, and closing the gap on the NHL’s elite.
items.body: We’ve written a lot over the years about an Oilers team that needed to get “one win better” after the 2024 Final, or find “just a few more periods of winning hockey” after losing to Florida again in 2025. Of course, it doesn’t work quite that way. When you win six playoff series in two years, you’re obviously doing most things right. The Leafs have won just eight playoff rounds this century, Vancouver nine, Montreal 13, and Calgary five. Edmonton has been elite, but still, Florida had something that they did not. You can’t change out your entire roster, but you can change how your roster plays. That’s what Mike Babcock is in the process of doing these days. The same players, mostly, are playing a different brand of hockey. And if there is one surprise in Edmonton, it’s that almost all of them are succeeding at the transition. That Babcock separated Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl for the first time all season Tuesday in Sunrise, and Edmonton scored four goals plus an empty-netter, is bad news for the rest of hockey. For one night at least, it wasn’t entirely the McDavid, Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard show. The Oilers beat Florida with two scoring lines, the best power play in hockey, depth players who won their shifts, a perfect penalty kill and better goaltending than Jacob Markstrom gave the Panthers. Sure, Florida was missing Sasha Barkov and Brad Machand), and tired after a long run of games.
